articles.title: DIY Home Security vs. Professionally Installed Systems: Which is Right for You?
articles.subtitle: Securing your home is essential for protecting your loved ones and property. But should you stick to DIY home security measures or invest in a professional system?
articles.summary: Securing your home helps protect people and property. Choosing between DIY security and a professionally installed system comes down to budget, how hands‑on you want to be, and the features you need. FBI reporting indicates burglary fell ~8.6% in 2024; national estimates suggest roughly 2,000 burglaries/day - about once every 40-45 seconds.
articles.mainContent:
Adoption is widespread: about 43% of U.S. internet households own a security solution, and nearly one‑third subscribe to a security service. Exact totals vary with methodology and definitions, so percentages are safer than household counts.

What Are DIY Home Security Systems?

DIY systems (Vivint, ADT Self Setup, SimpliSafe) typically include entry and motion sensors, a hub/base station, a siren, and optional cameras. You install the gear yourself and manage it via a mobile app. Many brands offer kits or let you build your own mix of devices.

Pros of DIY

  • Lower upfront costs & control: You choose devices and install on your schedule.

  • Customizable & scalable: Add or swap components over time.

  • Monitoring options: Many DIY brands offer self‑monitoring and 24/7 professional monitoring as an upgrade (no long‑term contracts for some).

Cons of DIY

  • Time & placement matter: You handle setup, sensor placement, and troubleshooting.

  • Network dependence: DIY systems rely on your home’s Wi‑Fi or cellular connection, so if your signal drops, some features may not work as expected.

  • False‑alarm exposure: Misplaced sensors or motion settings can cause nuisance alarms - some cities fine after repeated false alarms, so check local rules.

» Feeling overwhelmed? Here's how to choose the best home security system.

What Are Professionally Installed Systems?

Providers like Vivint and ADT design and install systems with options from basic sensors to integrated cameras, locks, and home automation - typically with 24/7 professional monitoring. A technician configures devices, optimizes placement, and walks you through the app.

Pros of Pro Install

  • Expert design & placement tailored to your home.

  • 24/7 monitoring to triage alarms and contact responders.

  • Smart‑home integrations & updates managed within the provider’s ecosystem.

Cons of Pro Install

  • Higher total cost: Equipment + installation fees + ongoing monitoring.

  • Monthly commitment: Most pro systems require a monitoring plan.

  • Bundled packages: You can customize, but add‑ons raise the price.

DIY vs. Pro: Budget & Ongoing Costs:

DIY home security systems typically have lower upfront prices because you install the equipment yourself, and monthly monitoring - if you choose it - tends to be more affordable. Professionally installed systems usually come with higher startup costs due to equipment packages and installation fees, along with ongoing monitoring contracts that can cost more each month. Overall, DIY offers more flexibility in how much you spend, while pro systems often bundle services and support into a higher but more hands‑off price.

DIY vs. Pro: Technical Expertise & Time

DIY home security systems usually come with clear instructions, support pages, and step‑by‑step guides to help you install everything on your own. Many use simple, “peel and stick” sensors and pre‑configured equipment to make setup quick and approachable. On the other hand, if you prefer a completely hands‑off experience - or you’re planning a more complex smart‑home setup - professional installation can take the work off your plate and ensure everything is configured for you.

Advanced Features & Typical Vulnerabilities

Some DIY systems place limits on how many third‑party devices they support, which can affect how easily you expand your setup or integrate it with a broader smart‑home ecosystem. Wireless systems can also face rare risks such as signal interference, though reputable models typically include features like anti‑jam detection and cellular backup to keep communication stable. It’s also worth noting that false alarms can occur with any system and may lead to local fines or permit requirements, so it’s important to check your city’s rules. In addition, some premium monitoring options combine AI‑enhanced video analysis with live human intervention for real‑time responses, though these services often come at a higher monthly cost.

Customization & Scalability

DIY platforms generally let you add devices freely over time. Vivint and ADT offer bundles and build‑your‑own paths; you can expand later, though costs rise with additional devices and pro visits.

How to Install a DIY Home Security System (Quick Guide)

  • Map risk areas: Prioritize entry doors, first‑floor windows, the garage, and blind spots.

  • Select components: Door/window contacts, motion sensors, keypad/hub, siren, cameras, and optional hazard sensors.

  • Secure your network: Use strong Wi‑Fi passwords and enable encryption; consider cellular backup.

  • Follow the brand guide: Place and test each device immediately after install.

  • Power & access: Choose battery vs. outlet; ensure easy access for maintenance.

  • Camera placement: Cover front door, garage/driveway, main living areas, and package drop‑off zones while respecting privacy.

  • Test & tune: Regularly test sensor zones and adjust camera motion settings to reduce false alerts.

  • Know local rules: Some cities require alarm permits and fine for repeated false alarms.

» Check out these 10 expert tips for installing home security cameras.

Location Risk: When Pro Monitoring Makes Sense

If you live in a higher‑burglary‑rate state (e.g., New Mexico), consider professional monitoring and stronger visible deterrents (sirens, lighting, doorbell cameras). Rankings vary year to year, but recent FBI‑based roundups still place New Mexico among the highest.

» Worried about break-ins? These are the signs that your house is marked by robbers.

Insurance Considerations

Some insurers offer homeowners discounts for professionally monitored systems or protective devices. Requirements and amounts vary by carrier; ask your insurer for details and a monitoring certificate if applicable.

Bottom Line

  • Choose DIY if you want lower upfront costs, flexibility, and you’re comfortable placing and maintaining devices.

  • Choose Pro install if you prefer expert design, always‑on monitoring, and turnkey support - even if it costs more.

  • Whichever route you pick, verify current prices on provider sites and check local false‑alarm rules to avoid unnecessary fees.

articles.title: 10 Critical Things I Always Do After Moving to a New House
articles.subtitle: Moving to a new home is an exciting adventure but often comes with its fair share of stress.
articles.summary: Moving to a new home is an exciting adventure but often comes with its fair share of stress.
articles.mainContent:
When it comes to your new home, feeling safe in your home is one of the most important aspects to consider. By integrating a good home security system into your moving process, you'll make your new home experience feel so much better.

Use the strategies below to assess what you need before you move, on moving day, as well as things to consider in the months after you've moved in but are still getting fully settled.

1. Get a home security system

Home security systems are installed can be professionally or with a DIY kit. These systems often include door and window sensors, motion detectors, and even security cameras.

Installing a home security system in a new home enhances safety, deters potential burglars, and provides peace of mind by monitoring for emergencies like break-ins, fires, and carbon monoxide leaks.

Each home has different needs: When we moved into our home we decided to add some security cameras as there were areas around the home that we couldn't see as well from inside. Knowing this, we selected a security system that would allow us to have the sensors we wanted, as well as the security camera views, all from the same app on our phone.

2. Have the locks re-keyed

It's best to change the locks on your new house right away. You never know who might have a key, even if you're not worried about the previous owner.

Scheduling a locksmith to visit or, if you feel comfortable doing it yourself, changing the locks yourself is a good idea. All interior and exterior doors to your home, as well as the windows, should have their locks rekeyed.

If you have a home warranty, check with them to see if they cover this service. I was able to have a home completely re-keyed for no cost, as my home warranty included a one-time re-keying of the home as part of their coverage.

3. Do a full walkthrough

It's a good idea to walk through your new home before moving. Seeing the house as a blank slate allows you to envision how your personal belongings will fit in, especially if it was staged when you first saw it. Bring a tape measure to help you plan more precisely where things like furniture will go.

Not only should you use the walkthrough as a vision board, but it's also crucial to remember that all of the conditions of the sale were fulfilled. Verify that all agreed-upon repairs have been made, all appliances that were supposed to stay (or be removed), and the outlets, switches, and other fixtures are in good working order.

4. Setup your utilities and connectivity

As part of your moving checklist, you should make sure that your utilities (electricity, gas, and water) are set up so they are ready for your move-in date because you probably don't want to spend your first night in your new home in the dark. In addition to standard utilities, think about internet, Wi-Fi, a phone line, and cable.

Depending on how far you're moving, some companies will let you transfer service from one location to another, especially if the company serves both addresses, but other times you'll need to completely cancel one location before starting over at another.

5. Have the house cleaned

When your house is empty, there is no better time to clean it thoroughly. It's worth a scrub down if you have the time between closing and the point at which your home is overrun with moving boxes.

Even if you build or purchase a new construction home, there are still elements of construction debris that are left behind, and having the home deep cleaned will help you and your family settle in comfortably.

6. Plan for where things will go

Spending time thinking about where things will go will help make the move-in process go smoother.

As you've seen your new home as a blank slate, use this time to think about how you and your family, will want to use the space. It's important to consider where things that you use every day will be located - for example, where is the best place to hang jackets? or leave shoes by the door?

Once you've made the plan, it's time to start unpacking!

7. Locate important spots in the home

Hope for the best, but be ready for the worst, as the saying goes. The worst time to search for your circuit breaker in a new house is right after the power has abruptly gone out.

Keep track of where the main water valve, fuse box, or circuit breakers are as you move in. Similar to cleaning, these should be much easier to locate when the home is empty. Make a note of the locations of your smoke and carbon monoxide detectors and test them to ensure they are working properly.

A home we recently purchased actually had 2 circuit breaker panels, and I was able to use the time before moving in to locate what items were wired to each panel, as well as ensure they were labeled correctly, making future troubleshooting and electrical work much easier and less stressful. We also identified the need to add smoke detector, which was quickly and easily done before we moved in.

Answer a few quick questions to find the right home security system for you Get Started

8. Explore your new community

Take a walk or drive around your new neighborhood to explore when you need a break from unpacking; focus not only on your neighborhood but also the amenities and attractions that are close by. Find the shops, community centers, and tourist attractions that will become your family's new favorite hangouts.

There are numerous social platforms available for connections specific to a given neighborhood. Find out what's going on in your new neighborhood by joining those.

Getting to know your neighbors is not a lost art, and being cordial with your neighbors can help your new home feel more like a home. You don't have to go door to door (Though that still works!), but just taking time to say hello as you see a new face can go a long way.

9. Sign up with the local neighborhood watch

While there are various apps and social platforms to get alerts about going on in your neighborhood, there's still tremendous value in joining your local neighborhood watch.

You can search the National Neighborhood Watch database to find your local law enforcement agency. Reach out to them for more info on the local neighborhood watch and how you can get signed up and start attending meetings as a volunteer. They likely have a notification system that will keep you updated on the meetings and happenings around you.

We found this to be a great way to both learn about our new community as well as meet people who lived there. Getting to know these people gave us a better connection with them and we were able to feel much safer about our new community.

10. Have an emergency plan

When it comes to emergency preparedness, it's never too early to start planning. Establish a plan of action for each family member's escape in the event of a fire. Create a plan of action and a place to shelter if you relocate to an area prone to natural disasters like tornadoes, hurricanes, or earthquakes.

When you draft your plan, be sure to include things such as phone numbers for your home security system, neighbors, phone number and location of the closest hospital, contact info for the fire department, police department, and more.

Securing Your Home First

As you can see, many things go into ensuring that you have safety and security as you get settled in your new home and community. If you decide to install a security system yourself, companies like SimpliSafe and Cove are there to help along the way. They can help with the traditional sensors and detectors needed to protect your home and provide solutions that integrate with various smart home offerings.

After moving, don't feel that you must complete everything by yourself, or right away. Getting used to a new home can take time.

articles.metaDescription: When it comes to selecting a home security system there are various factors to consider and steps to take in order to ensure you select the right system for your needs.
articles.title: How to Choose the Best Home Security System for Your Home
articles.subtitle: Choosing the perfect security system for your home is a vital step in safeguarding what matters most to you.
articles.summary: Choosing the perfect security system for your home is a vital step in safeguarding what matters most to you.
articles.mainContent:
A home security system, along with conspicuous signage, is a powerful deterrent against crime. In fact, nearly 60% of burglars will steer clear of homes with visible security measures in place.

To keep your home safe, you need a reliable security system that offers the right level of protection and shields you from potential threats. But with so many options available, you need to know exactly what to look for.

In this post, we've listed the most important features to consider and compiled a step-by-step guide to help you choose the best home security system for your home.

Answer a few quick questions to find the right home security system for you Get Started

4 Factors to Consider Before Choosing a Home Security System

The best security system for your home will meet your specific safety requirements, fit your budget and offer the support you need. To make an informed decision, consider the following factors:

User-Friendliness

Choose a system that's easy to operate. Anyone living in your home should be able to use it, including individuals with limitations or special requirements.

System Type

There are various options to choose from, including wired, wireless, monitored, and unmonitored systems. Take the time to evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of each system type before making your final decision.

For example, wireless systems will generally be more reliable, while wired systems are more affordable and easier to install.

Additionally, decide whether you prefer a DIY installation or professional assistance.

Cost Considerations

Home security system costs can vary greatly, so it's important to determine your budget before selecting a system. Consider both the upfront expenses and ongoing fees, such as monthly monitoring charges.

Also, make sure to understand the renewal terms and requirements of the system and any potential implications of adding extra sensors or detectors.

Customer Support

Look for a provider that offers reliable customer support and technical assistance, including 24/7 monitoring and availability through online chat or a customer service hotline.

7 Steps to Choosing the Best Home Security System

1. Assess Your Security Needs

Start by evaluating your home's vulnerabilities and identifying potential entry points for burglars. This will help you determine what type(s) of sensors and detectors you may need.

2. Research Available Options

Because many different types of home security systems are available, look for reviews and recommendations from trusted sources to help narrow down your options.

3. Consider Your Budget

The cost of a home security system can vary widely depending on the type of system you choose and the level of monitoring you require. Determine how much you're willing to spend and find options within your budget.

4. Look for Additional Features

Some home security systems come with additional features such as video monitoring, smart home integration, mobile app control via smartphone, and lockout prevention features like keyless entry and remote access. Determine which features are important to you and your family and look for systems that offer them.

5. Check for Compatibility

If you already have smart home devices such as cameras, doorbells, or sensors, make sure that the security system you choose is compatible with these devices.

6. Choose a Reputable Provider

Choose a reputable provider with a proven track record of delivering high-quality security systems and excellent customer service. Check for customer reviews and ratings to gauge the provider's reliability and trustworthiness.

7. Install and Test the System

Once you've chosen a home security system, make sure it's properly installed and test it to ensure it's working correctly. Set up notifications and alerts to stay informed about any potential security breaches.

Finding the Right Security System for Your Home

To find a home security system that caters to your family's needs, aligns with your budget, and provides peace of mind, carefully consider the factors and steps outlined above. Choosing the ideal security system for your home will require thorough research and thoughtful deliberation—so you can make an informed decision.

articles.metaTitle: 10 Essential Recovery Steps for Package Theft
articles.metaDescription: Discover effective strategies for dealing with stolen packages. Follow our 10-step guide to recover your items and prevent future thefts quickly.
articles.title: 10 Steps to Take if Your Package Is Stolen
articles.subtitle: Just stepped onto your porch to find your package missing? Don't panic—with the right tools and a few critical steps, you can catch porch pirates red-handed, recover stolen items, get compensation, or have your package resent.
articles.summary: Just stepped onto your porch to find your package missing? Don't panic—with the right tools and a few critical steps, you can catch porch pirates red-handed, recover stolen items, get compensation, or have your package resent.
articles.mainContent:
With over 20 years of experience in home security systems, I understand the frustration of a stolen package. In 2023, 49 million Americans were victims of porch piracy. Most insurance policies cover stolen deliveries, but getting compensation requires quick, proper action.

I'll use my industry knowledge to provide a 10-step guide on what to do after a high-value theft from your property. You can build a compelling reimbursement case by gathering documents, filing timely claims, and using home security tech.

» Here's how to choose the best home security system to protect your property.

1. Contact the Shipping Company

If you think your package has been stolen, review your purchase confirmation email for a tracking number to monitor its shipping status. Delivery companies often have real-time tracking, which allows for up-to-date notifications on your delivery's location.

If the status shows it was delivered and you can't find it, contact the shipping company (USPS, UPS, FedEx) to file a claim. Provide your contact details, delivery date, tracking number, package contents, value, and supporting documents like receipts and invoices.

2. Notify the Seller or Retailer

If your package appears stolen, contact the retailer or seller that sold you the item. Retailers have different policies for handling stolen packages. Still, you are typically entitled to a refund or replacement under most policies.

If you purchased the item on Amazon from a third-party Amazon Seller, contact them and attempt to resolve the issue. Suppose you're still waiting for a response after two business days or find the seller uncooperative. In that case, you can file an A-to-Z Guarantee claim. 

3. Contact Your Neighbors

Ask your neighbors if they saw the delivery or have your package. They may have brought it inside to keep it safe from theft or weather. Neighbors can also help watch for weird activities caught on security cameras and report anything unusual. Leverage your community to help locate missing packages and stay alert to potential thieves.

4. Check Surveillance Footage

A 2023 nationwide survey found that external cameras were listed as the most important security system feature by 32.3% of respondents. If you have a video surveillance system, review the footage to see if you can identify the thief or gather more information about the incident.

Remember that some video systems only store recordings for a specified period before overwriting. Contacting a home security company like ADT or Vivint can help you access and preserve valuable surveillance footage related to the theft.

5. Document the Theft

Take photos of the area where the package was stolen, any signs of forced entry, and any related damage. Having a home security system like SimpliSafe can assist in providing video footage to document the theft.

This documentation can be useful for insurance claims or investigations. Taking swift action can help the investigation process and increase the chances of recovering your stolen package or receiving compensation through insurance.

Keep detailed records of all your communications and interactions related to the incident. If you need clarification on any specific steps, consider consulting with your home security company, like ADT alternatives, the shipping carrier, or legal professionals, for guidance tailored to your situation.

6. File a Police Report

You should report the theft to your local law enforcement agency. Provide them with as much information as possible, like the tracking number, package contents, and any surveillance footage from your home security cameras. Many police departments allow you to file a police report online.

The specific website will vary based on location. Still, you'll likely find the appropriate place to report your stolen package by searching Google for "[your town/city] online police report."

7. Use Your Credit Card's Purchase Protection Feature

A credit card's purchase protection usually covers theft and damage to a physical item within a set time after you bought it. To make a claim, you must have purchased the item with the credit card you are filing with. You can check the website to see if you have this coverage.

Remember that some credit card companies don't cover high-value items (typically over $500 to $1,000). You may need to file a police report before they refund you. Purchase protection often only covers you after using your primary insurance, like homeowners' or renters' insurance.

8. Check Your Insurance Coverage

The amount your home or renter's insurance company pays for stolen packages depends on your policy and provider. Typically, there are coverage limits:

  • Coverage cap: Your policy likely has a maximum total payout for all stolen possessions. If you reach this cap, no further coverage is available.
  • Category limits: Your insurance may cap coverage for high-value items like electronics or jewelry, even if the total cap isn't met.
  • Deductible: The amount you pay out-of-pocket on a claim before insurance coverage starts. If your loss is less than your deductible, your insurance does not pay.
  • Valuation basis: Payouts may be based on items' depreciated actual cash value or current replacement cost.

How Can Insurance Help Recover High-Value Packages?

When a high-value item is stolen from your property, insurance providers can play a vital role in mitigating the impact of the theft. Here's how:

  • Insurance can provide financial compensation if you have the right coverage if a high-value package is stolen from your doorstep.
  • Many policies specifically cover theft from a property. Check if this risk is covered by your provider. 
  • File a police report promptly as proof of loss. This is usually required to submit a theft claim.
  • Know your deductible and coverage limits, which determine the compensation amount. Ensure limits cover high-value items.
  • Insurers may offer discounted premiums if you use preventative measures like security cameras and secure delivery.
  • For precious items, specialized policies with comprehensive coverage may be available.
  • Insurance companies tend to prioritize and respond rapidly to claims for high-value thefts.

» Understand the difference between home warranty vs home home insurance.

9. Monitor for Suspicious Activity

Keep an eye on your financial accounts and personal information. Stolen packages may be part of larger identity theft schemes. If so, consider contacting a trusted identity theft protection service to assist you. 

If you've noticed unfamiliar people on the street or strange cars parked on corners—these could be signs your house has been marked by robbers for future theft. If you see this suspicious activity in your neighborhood, the police may be more likely to investigate. 

10. Consider Prevention Measures Against Porch Piracy

According to a recent survey, 49% of consumers worry that their online orders may get stolen from their doorstep. To protect your packages from porch pirates, consider implementing the following these measures:

  • Install security cameras: Set up cameras around your property to deter thieves and capture any incidents of theft. 
  • Use secure delivery options: Choose delivery lockers or require signature confirmation for your packages to reduce the risk of them being stolen.
  • Invest in shipping insurance: For high-value items like electronics, consider purchasing shipping insurance through the vendor or delivery service.
  • Home monitoring system: Install a system like Cove for 24/7 monitoring and remote access. This is an excellent way to protect your home while you're on vacation. 
  • Arrange for alternate delivery locations: Have your packages delivered to your workplace or a trusted neighbor's house, especially if you know you won't be home.

Outsmart Porch Pirates, Stop Package Theft

Stolen online orders are a growing problem that can leave you missing your much-anticipated packages. Remember to take preventative measures like tracking all deliveries so you know when they arrive. Also, review your homeowner’s insurance to confirm coverage for stolen items. 

You can deter thieves and capture evidence by installing home security systems. With doorbell cameras and real-time mobile alerts—you can guard against package theft and get your long-awaited packages.

articles.title: 10 Expert Tips for Installing Discreet Home Security Cameras
articles.subtitle: After over two decades in the security industry, I've learned how to seamlessly integrate cameras into a home environment to increase your safety without compromising the aesthetics of your space.
articles.summary: After over two decades in the security industry, I've learned how to seamlessly integrate cameras into a home environment to increase your safety without compromising the aesthetics of your space.
articles.mainContent:
Home security systems are more than just a precaution; they're a necessity. Consider this: In 2022, the US reported 269.8 burglaries per 100,000 people. This statistic emphasizes the urgent need to secure your home.

As a seasoned certified security project manager (CSPM) with 20+ years of experience in the field, I specialize in effective home protection. In this guide, I'll provide 10 expert tips for installing discreet home security cameras. These insights can help protect your property and give your family the peace of mind they deserve.

» Relocating soon? Here are 10 critical things I always do after moving to a new house.

1. Blend Your Cameras With Your Home Environment

When installing discreet security cameras, balancing visibility with your home's style is crucial. I prefer cameras that subtly blend with their surroundings. Brands like Scout Alarm provide sleek, compact options ideal for this purpose. These cameras are modest enough not to stand out, yet effective in keeping your dwelling secure.

For modern homes, their minimalist designs can complement contemporary architecture without being obtrusive. But if your home has a more traditional style, opt for cameras that can be disguised as everyday objects. The goal is to maintain the safety of your home while preserving its aesthetic appeal.

2. Place Cameras Higher for Optimal Coverage

Install your home security cameras at least eight feet above the ground, out of reach for most people standing on the ground. This height reduces the chances of someone tampering with the device.

ADT can help you choose the best spots for camera placement. With their guidance, you can effectively prevent tampering and cover a wider area, making your security system more efficient and reliable.

3. Hide Your Camera Wiring for a Cleaner Look

Hide your security camera wiring to protect it from tampering and damage. These wires are essential for camera functionality, and safeguarding them helps ensure your security system runs smoothly. Concealed wires reduce the chances of vandalism and environmental harm while keeping your home tidy.

Hiding wires also makes your security system less noticeable to potential intruders. This may require extra effort, such as running cables through walls or using decorations for cover. Still, it's a valuable step for maintaining a secure and discreet surveillance setup.

» Decide on the best fit for your home: wired vs. wireless home security systems.

4. Strategically Position Cameras in Hidden Areas

Cover main areas like the front door and driveway, but also consider less obvious spots where intruders may be able to hide. Assess dimly lit areas around windows or doors and places like workshops where you keep valuables. Other important locations you should cover include:

  • Back and side doors
  • Off-street windows
  • Common areas, like living rooms or kitchens
  • Garage
  • Front and back yard
  • Basement
  • Second-floor windows

Weigh the costs of home security. Investing in comprehensive coverage from a top-notch provider can significantly boost your home's security. This investment typically costs less than potential losses from a break-in. Plus, actively adding cameras to overlooked areas ensures complete protection across your property.

5. Install Motion Activated Lights

Integrate motion-activated lights with your system to enhance footage quality, especially at night. Cameras such as SimpliSafe's Wireless Outdoor Security Camera come with motion-activated lighting. This feature ensures that the area under surveillance is well-lit whenever there's movement.

Motion-activated lights can improve camera visibility and deter potential intruders. The sudden illumination can also startle and discourage them while providing your camera with enough light to record effectively.

6. Sync Your Cameras With Smart Home Devices

Connect your security cameras to your smart home system for enhanced convenience and efficiency. With this integration, you can record with a voice command or have cameras record automatically when an alarm triggers. You can also view live feeds and receive alerts through a single app on your phone.

For example, Frontpoint Security's Hub and Keypad are central control systems. They let you monitor your home security and control all smart devices, including Alexa and Google Home, using just one app.

» Here are 10 signs your home could be a target for robbers.

7. Use Privacy Film to Conceal Cameras

Apply privacy film on your home windows to enhance daytime security and privacy. This film makes it difficult for outsiders to see inside your home, including spotting the presence of security cameras. While it's less effective when indoor lights are on at night, it's an excellent solution for sunny days.

As a bonus, it reflects sunlight and heat, keeping your home cooler and cutting air conditioning costs. It can also help protect your interiors from UV damage.

The film is available in various designs and tints, allowing you to choose one that complements your home's style. Focus on more exposed areas, such as street-facing rooms or glass doors, for enhanced privacy.

8. Choose Solar-Powered Cameras for Remote Areas

Install solar-powered cameras with battery backup in locations where hardwiring isn't feasible, like remote gates, workshops, or detached garages.

Solar panels provide a reliable power source without complex wiring, ideal for remote or hard-to-reach areas. They ensure sustainable power, and the battery backup keeps them operational, even on cloudy days or at night.

Wyze Home Security offers solar-powered cameras that are easy to install and maintain, eliminating the need for long cables or frequent battery replacements.

9. Opt for IR Cameras for Discreet Night Monitoring

Use infrared (IR) illumination in your hidden home security cameras—like those offered by Cove—to enhance low-light surveillance. These cameras can record high-resolution video in dark conditions, ensuring that any footage you capture at night is clear and usable.

The IR light is also invisible to the human eye, meaning you can observe movement without alerting or assisting intruders. This technology allows you to discreetly monitor your property after dark without attracting attention.

10. Cover Indicator Lights on Cameras

To keep your security cameras unnoticeable, especially at night, cover their indicator lights. Systems like Frontpoint Security often offer options to control these flashes, helping you maintain a low profile for your surveillance equipment.

A University of North Carolina at Charlotte study reveals that about 60% of burglars avoid homes with visible security systems. Discreet camera installation provides a strategic advantage. Burglars who are unaware of surveillance are less likely to take measures to avoid being recorded, leading to more effective security footage.

Boost Your Home Security With Smart Camera Choices

Choosing discreet camera installation can streamline your home security and prepare you for the future. Trends show a rising interest in subtle, smartly integrated surveillance systems. Advancements in AI make these cameras increasingly adept at threat detection. It's a smart investment for your safety and peace of mind.

articles.subtitle: Want to make your home safer and more convenient? The latest integration of home automation and security takes guarding to cutting-edge levels.

articles.mainContent:
With 20+ years of experience in home security, I've seen firsthand how technology can better protect what matters most—your family. Since burglaries across the US occur every 30 seconds, you need innovative tools with customized alerts, cameras, sensors, and more.

In this article, I'll explain how today's smart home systems and providers can work together to automate and monitor your property. You can give your loved ones convenience and peace of mind with the right approach.

» Feeling overwhelmed? Learn how to choose the best home security system.

5 Things You Can Do With Smart Home Automation

Control Your Lighting

Home automation lets you easily manage your home's ambiance and energy efficiency with smart lighting. Brands like ADT offer a range of smart bulbs that integrate seamlessly into any home setup.

You can program your system to turn on all exterior lights if a door is opened at night when the alarm is armed. If it's daytime, it can trigger a siren instead.

Adjust the Temperature

With smart thermostats from companies like Vivint, you can keep your home comfortable while saving on energy bills. These devices learn your habits and schedule to adjust the temperature based on your preferences.

They also use geofencing, which sets a virtual boundary around a geographical area to trigger specific actions when a device enters or exits that zone. This feature can help conserve power when you're away.

Use Voice Activation

Voice-activated assistants like Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant allow you to control your smart home effortlessly. You can request music and weather updates or manage other smart devices completely hands-free.

Linking these intelligent helpers with your security setup also boosts safety. If intruders enter your home, voice commands notify them that the system is activated, letting criminals know you're aware of their presence.

Lock and Unlock Your Doors From Anywhere

Did you know that 34% of burglars enter a home through the front door? Luckily, you can secure your doors remotely with SimpliSafe's smart locks. The SimpliLock feature automatically locks entryways on a set schedule, which is handy if you forget your unique code.

You'll be notified if someone enters the wrong PIN code five times. And after 15 failed attempts, the system automatically deadbolts for 30 minutes. Locking your door via a smartphone app, voice command, or keyless entry system offers considerable convenience.

Stay Connected to Your Property Remotely

Home automation enables remote access and control of your home, whether you're in another room or away on a trip. Apps from providers like FrontPoint Security let you check live footage, adjust lighting settings, and receive immediate notifications if an alarm goes off.

Top home security systems facilitate round-the-clock real-time monitoring with smart alerts that keep you connected. You can view high-quality video feeds of your property from your phone at any time.

How Home Automation and Security Systems Improve Your Safety

Outdoor and Indoor Security Cameras Deter Crime

Installing security cameras inside and outside your house is one of the best ways to ward off criminals. A survey conducted with inmates found that visible security cameras deter robberies.

Advanced home security systems provide multiple lines of defense against intruders. For example, Cove has a sleek video doorbell to see and speak with visitors, no matter where you are.

I recommend strategically placing weatherproof cameras around the exterior of your home to capture clear footage and monitor all angles of your property. Consider tips for installing discreet home cameras that blend into your walls seamlessly. This way, you can unobtrusively check for any suspicious activity.

Detect Motion With Sensors and Security Systems

If you're wondering how to secure your windows and doors—these smart devices are your answer. Infrared sensors from companies pick up body heat and movement in the protected area day or night. These scanners also have adjustable settings to prevent false alarms triggered by pets or other disturbances.

Plus, they can automatically activate security cameras to start recording when an intrusion occurs. Vivint's motion detectors even use military-grade radar technology to spot people when they aren't moving, which is ideal for catching burglars attempting to hide.

Automatically Thwart Intruders With Light and Sound

Innovative setups can automatically activate lights and sound alarms if they detect a trespasser, creating a presence when you're away. Voice alarms that clearly announce an active security system can also deter would-be intruders.

In addition, 24/7 professional monitoring ensures safety without requiring you to activate anything manually. You can rely on these intelligent features to protect your home when you're on vacation.

Secure Your Garage Door

With a smart controller, you'll receive notifications whenever your garage door opens. If you accidentally leave your garage exposed, you can immediately close and lock it using your smartphone—even if you're miles away from home. This allows you to keep your garage and its contents secure.

Protect You in Environmental Emergencies

Smart home devices can protect you in environmental emergencies. Smoke detectors and carbon monoxide alarms will notify you of fire hazards and trigger automatic safety measures.

For example, HVAC systems can automatically shut off to slow the spread of flames. Doors can also unlock to allow quick exit while giving emergency responders easy access.

Prevent Package Theft

Package theft has become extremely common. Over 75% of Americans had a package stolen in 2023. A video doorbell camera from providers like Scout Alarm can instantly record deliveries and notify you of drop-offs. 

With two-way audio, you can also communicate with visitors from wherever you are. This deters potential thieves and ensures that your packages and belongings won't go missing.

Enjoy Convenience With Automated Home Security

Receive Customizable Alerts and Notifications

Providers like Link Home Security let you personalize your alert settings to suit your needs. Customizable notifications can inform you when doors or windows are opened, motion is detected, or other significant events happen. You can specify which incidents trigger alerts to ensure you only receive notifications that are relevant to you.

It Creates Event Logs and Historical Data

In addition to real-time updates, home security systems create detailed activity logs and records. These provide invaluable insight into what happens on your property over time.

Review event histories to understand traffic patterns, enhance security measures, and even aid investigations if breaches occur. This is especially useful if there are signs that robbers have marked your house.

Control Everything From One Hub

Smart home security usually includes a central hub that connects all your sensors to monitoring stations. These are typically touchscreen panels mounted to a wall that you can use to arm or disarm your system.

You can also view recorded or live video footage on security cameras or video doorbells, turn lights on and off, or adjust your temperature. Options like ADT's Google Nest Hub include daily schedules and reminders, an entertainment center, and even sleep-sensing technology.

6 Steps to Set Up Your Automated Security System

  1. Get compatible system hardware: Purchase an automated setup from services like Vivint, ADT, or SimpliSafe that includes a hub/panel, sensors for doors and motion, and cameras. Ensure your gear works with any virtual assistants already in your home.
  2. Strategically place sensors and cameras: Position motion sensors near entryways (internal and external) to catch comings and goings. Place them on any open window or door to monitor breaches. Also, focus cameras outdoors and in high-traffic rooms.
  3. Set automation rules and alerts: Use the security app to configure rules like "If the front door opens while we're away, text me." Set emergency contacts to notify if alarms go off.
  4. Connect camera feeds and controls: Link your cameras and security panel to any smart displays to pull recent footage or arm/disarm the system using voice commands.
  5. Consider pro monitoring: Security providers like FrontPoint offer professional monitoring services, which dispatch emergency responders when alerts occur.
  6. Update and add users over time: Give family members access codes and download security apps to their phones to control and monitor your system. 

Enhance Your Safety With Home Automation and Security Systems

Even if you live in one of the five safest cities in the US, installing a home security system can provide extra protection and peace of mind. Whether it's a basic option with entry sensors or a high-tech setup with facial recognition—automation puts control back in your hands.

Home Security Systems in 2026: What They Are and Why They Matter

A home security system is a network of devices - like sensors, cameras, and alarms - that helps detect threats and alert you quickly, often through an app and optional 24/7 professional monitoring. In 2026, it’s especially important because modern systems deliver real-time mobile alerts, smart home integration, and faster confirmation (like video) so you can respond right away whether you’re home or away.

What is the best home security system: DIY or professional install?

The best home security system depends on your needs, budget, and comfort with technology. In 2026, both professionally installed and DIY home security systems offer robust protection, smart integrations, and access to features like mobile monitoring, wireless connectivity, and fire or flood detection. But which is better for your home?

DIY home security systems: affordable and flexible

DIY home security systems are wireless setups you can install yourself in under an hour. These systems often include peel-and-stick sensors, smart cameras, and optional monitoring subscriptions.

Why choose a DIY system?

  • No installation fees - Avoid paying $100–$300 for professional setup

  • Portable - Ideal for renters or people who move often

  • Smart home ready - Easily integrates with Alexa, Google Assistant, or Apple HomeKit

  • Scalable - Add more cameras, sensors, or smart locks anytime

  • Lower monthly costs - Many offer optional or cheaper self-monitoring plans

These systems are built for modern living. You install the sensors on entry points, set up indoor and outdoor security cameras, and connect everything to an app on your phone. No need for drilling or rewiring - most devices are battery-powered and mount in minutes.

Professionally installed home security systems: hands-off and reliable

Professional systems involve in-home setup by trained technicians. They're ideal for large homes, high-security needs, or users who prefer a "set it and forget it" approach.

Benefits of professional install:

  • Expert placement - Installers maximise coverage and minimise blind spots

  • Included warranties - Hardware is usually covered for repairs or replacements

  • Professional monitoring - 24/7 call centres contact you or dispatch authorities during emergencies

  • Service guarantees - Includes tech support, maintenance, and system checks

However, professional systems often involve contracts (12–36 months) and higher up-front costs. The installation itself may require drilling or wiring, making them less portable for renters.

Which is more secure: DIY or professional home alarms?

Security-wise, both systems can be effective - if used properly. What matters most is whether the system is armed, monitored, and has motion sensors and cameras in the right places.

Key considerations:

  • Monitoring type - DIY often relies on self-monitoring unless you upgrade

  • Connectivity - Most modern systems are wireless with cellular or WiFi backup

  • Power failure protection - Backup batteries are standard

  • Response time - Professional monitoring ensures someone calls authorities if you can't

In short, both systems can protect your home well - but professional monitoring adds a layer of reliability in emergencies.

Understanding the structure of alarm systems helps you choose the right setup:

  1. Local alarm systems - Not connected to a central service. Sounds loud alarm if triggered.

  2. Wired alarm systems - Sensors connected via cables to a central control panel, often monitored.

  3. Wireless alarm systems - Use radio signals to communicate between sensors and control panel.

Any of these can include professional or self-monitoring services, depending on the provider.

Installation tips for better camera coverage

Correct installation is key to capturing clear footage and deterring intruders.

  • Mount cameras 5-6 feet high for optimal face visibility

  • Tilt downward at 10-15 degrees to capture full torsos

  • Use wide-angle lenses to cover large rooms or entry points

  • Place outdoor security cameras at entryways, garages, driveways, and rear doors

  • Angle staircase cameras to capture both top and bottom landings
